moduleInfo.title: Unlocking the World of Harry Potter: Auror Level
moduleInfo.subject: Literature/Fantasy

vocabulary.definition: An object in which a Dark wizard has hidden a fragment of his or her soul for the purpose of attaining immortality.
A witch or wizard who can transform himself or herself into an animal at will; this transformation ability is learned, not hereditary.
One who can speak and understand the language of snakes (Parseltongue), a rare skill often associated with Dark Wizards.
A skeletal, black, winged horse visible only to those who have witnessed death.
The magical art of closing one's mind against Legilimency (the intrusion of others) and mind manipulation.
The magical art of navigating through the mental landscape of another person, often referred to as 'mind-reading'.
A magical object charmed to transport anyone who touches it instantly to a specific destination.
An employee of the Department of Mysteries in the Ministry of Magic, dealing with confidential and often mysterious magical matters.
A shapeshifting non-being that takes on the form of whatever most frightens the person who encounters it.
A small, one-legged creature that appears to be made of wispy smoke, known for luring travellers into bogs with a lantern.
A magical item sold at Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes that creates an immediate, impenetrable black cloud when thrown.
A magical plant whose root is a powerful restorer; its cry is fatal to anyone who hears it when fully grown.
A complex charm used to conceal a secret, storing it within a single person, the Secret-Keeper.
A monstrous hybrid creature resulting from Hagrid breeding a Manticore with a Fire Crab.
An accidental side-effect of Apparition where part of the wizard's body is left behind.

timeline.event: Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington (Nearly Headless Nick) dies on October 31st.
Tom Riddle opens the Chamber of Secrets, resulting in the death of Myrtle Warren, and frames Rubeus Hagrid.
Albus Dumbledore defeats the Dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald in a duel.
James Potter, Lily Evans, Sirius Black, and Peter Pettigrew all start their first year at Hogwarts.
Harry Potter is born on July 31st.
Voldemort attacks the Potters in Godric's Hollow, killing James and Lily, and his curse rebounds on Harry, making him 'The Boy Who Lived'.
Harry Potter begins his first year at Hogwarts and stops Professor Quirrell from stealing the Philosopher's Stone.
The Chamber of Secrets is reopened, and Harry defeats the Basilisk and Tom Riddle's memory.
Harry participates in the Triwizard Tournament, which concludes with the rebirth of Lord Voldemort.
The Battle of Hogwarts takes place, resulting in the final defeat and death of Lord Voldemort.

artworks.title: A History of Magic
artworks.description: A standard school history book required for first-year students, penned by a prolific but dull wizarding historian.

artworks.title: Magical Me
artworks.description: A highly-embellished life story of a charming, yet fraudulent, celebrity wizard who was briefly a Defence Against the Dark Arts professor.

artworks.title: The Statute of Secrecy
artworks.description: A global piece of legislation enacted in the late 17th century to hide the existence of the wizarding world from Muggles.

artworks.title: The Fountain of Fair Fortune
artworks.description: A story from an ancient collection of wizarding folklore, involving three witches and a knight who seek happiness by bathing in an enchanted fountain.

artworks.title: The Marauder's Map
artworks.description: A seemingly blank piece of paper that, when activated with a phrase, reveals the entire grounds and all inhabitants of the wizarding school.

artworks.title: The Vanishing Cabinet
artworks.description: A set of two large wooden wardrobes that connect two distant locations, creating a hidden passageway between them.

artworks.title: The Half-Blood Prince's Textbook
artworks.description: An old school book with handwritten notes, spells, and corrections, which drastically improves its owner's ability in the subject.

artworks.title: The Deathly Hallows
artworks.description: Three mythical objects—a wand, a stone, and a cloak—that are said to grant their master power over Death itself.

locations.name: Godric's Hollow
locations.significance: The village where both Harry Potter and Albus Dumbledore's family once lived, and the site of Lily and James Potter's murder.

locations.name: Number 12, Grimmauld Place
locations.significance: The ancestral home of the Black family and the secret headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix.

locations.name: Azkaban
locations.significance: The terrible wizarding prison located on a remote island in the middle of the North Sea, guarded by Dementors.

locations.name: Spinner's End
locations.significance: The Muggle street and house where Professor Snape lives during the summer holidays.

locations.name: Gringotts Wizarding Bank
locations.significance: The goblin-run bank in Diagon Alley, famously the safest place in the wizarding world (except for Hogwarts).

locations.name: Little Hangleton
locations.significance: The Muggle village near the Riddle House and the home of Voldemort's maternal ancestors, the Gaunts.

locations.name: The Hog's Head Inn
locations.significance: A notoriously dingy pub in Hogsmeade run by Aberforth Dumbledore, used for the first D.A. meeting and as a safe escape route during the Battle of Hogwarts.

locations.name: The Department of Mysteries
locations.significance: The section of the Ministry of Magic containing various rooms dedicated to fundamental forces like Time, Space, and Death, where the Battle of the Department of Mysteries took place.

locations.name: Shell Cottage
locations.significance: The seaside home of Bill and Fleur Weasley, which served as a safe haven and refuge for Harry, Ron, and Hermione.

locations.name: The Chamber of Secrets
locations.significance: A hidden chamber beneath Hogwarts, housing a Basilisk and created by Salazar Slytherin to purge the school of Muggle-born students.

locations.name: Malfoy Manor
locations.significance: The lavish home of the Malfoy family, used as the Death Eaters' headquarters and a holding cell for prisoners during the Second Wizarding War.

locations.name: The Leaky Cauldron
locations.significance: A dark, shabby London pub that serves as the hidden entrance between the Muggle world and Diagon Alley.

locations.name: The Shrieking Shack
locations.significance: An abandoned building in Hogsmeade, infamous for being the most haunted in Britain, but actually used as a place for Remus Lupin to transform safely during the full moon.

locations.name: Ollivanders
locations.significance: The wand shop in Diagon Alley, established in 382 B.C., where Harry and many other students bought their first wand.

locations.name: Room of Requirement
locations.significance: A secret room in Hogwarts that only appears when a person is in genuine need, transforming itself into whatever the person requires.

trueFalse.statement: Neville Longbottom's parents were killed by Bellatrix Lestrange during the First Wizarding War.
trueFalse.correction: Neville's parents were tortured into insanity with the Cruciatus Curse, but they were not killed. They live at St. Mungo's Hospital.

trueFalse.statement: Dumbledore's Patronus is a phoenix, mirroring his beloved pet, Fawkes.
trueFalse.correction: Dumbledore's Patronus is a phoenix, but his pet Fawkes is not the reason; the phoenix Patronus appeared before he acquired Fawkes.

trueFalse.statement: The first name of Lord Voldemort's mother was Merope.
trueFalse.correction: Voldemort's mother's full name was Merope Gaunt, the last known descendant of Salazar Slytherin.

trueFalse.statement: The maximum number of turns Hermione was instructed to use on the Time-Turner was four, to prevent 'nasty side-effects'.
trueFalse.correction: The instructions were to turn the knob three times, and Hermione said that any more would cause them to travel too far back in time.

trueFalse.statement: The core of Harry Potter's first wand was a single Phoenix feather, donated by Fawkes.
trueFalse.correction: The core of Harry's wand came from the same phoenix, Fawkes, that provided the core for Voldemort's wand.

trueFalse.statement: The 'Mudblood' slur was first used in the books by Draco Malfoy to insult Hermione.
trueFalse.correction: The slur 'Mudblood' was first used by Draco Malfoy, but it was directed at Hermione, not used by her to insult someone.

trueFalse.statement: The Ministry of Magic's Auror Office is located on the second level of the Ministry's headquarters.
trueFalse.correction: The Auror Office is located on Level Two, but the Department of Magical Law Enforcement is located there, the Auror Office is inside that department.

trueFalse.statement: The password to the Headmaster's Office is always the name of a type of magical sweet.
trueFalse.correction: Dumbledore is known for using names of Muggle sweets like Sherbet Lemon and Cockroach Cluster as passwords.

trueFalse.statement: The second Horcrux Harry and Dumbledore destroy is Salazar Slytherin's locket.
trueFalse.correction: The second Horcrux Dumbledore and Harry sought to destroy was Slytherin's locket, but they only retrieved a fake locket; the real second Horcrux destroyed was the diary.

trueFalse.statement: The official colors of the Quidditch team Chudley Cannons are orange and purple.
trueFalse.correction: The Chudley Cannons, Ron Weasley's favorite team, wear orange robes with a cannon emblem.

trueFalse.statement: During the Triwizard Tournament, Fleur Delacour's sister, Gabrielle, was the person taken by the merpeople during the Second Task.
trueFalse.correction: Gabrielle Delacour was the person 'most dear' to Fleur and was taken to the bottom of the Black Lake.

trueFalse.statement: Gilderoy Lockhart's favorite color, as revealed in his autobiography, is lilac.
trueFalse.correction: Gilderoy Lockhart's favorite color is lavender, as mentioned in Chamber of Secrets, not lilac.

trueFalse.statement: The Black family house-elf, Kreacher, was killed during the Battle of Hogwarts.
trueFalse.correction: Kreacher survived the Battle of Hogwarts and led the house-elves to join the fight against the Death Eaters.

trueFalse.statement: The Hogwarts house that Filius Flitwick originally belonged to as a student was Ravenclaw.
trueFalse.correction: Flitwick, the Charms Master and Head of Ravenclaw House, was indeed a Ravenclaw student.

trueFalse.statement: The only Deathly Hallow that Harry Potter ultimately keeps is the Elder Wand.
trueFalse.correction: Harry kept the Invisibility Cloak, rejected the Resurrection Stone, and decided to let the Elder Wand’s power die with him.

quiz.question: What is the name of the magical alley where you can find Borgin and Burkes, which sells unusual and Dark objects?
What creature is on the top of the weather vane in the courtyard of the Burrow, the Weasley family home?
Who was the Headmaster of Hogwarts before Albus Dumbledore's tenure began?
What object did Harry first use to transport himself to the Leaky Cauldron after blowing up Aunt Marge?
What is the incantation for the Charm that lights up the tip of a wizard's wand, a spell first taught by Professor Flitwick?
What is the name of the Hippogriff that Harry saves from execution in his third year?
What is the name of the popular wizarding newspaper based in London, England?
What were the initials of the organization Hermione Granger founded to advocate for house-elf rights?
Who was the first person to successfully raise their wand to honor Albus Dumbledore after his death?
What flavor of Bertie Bott's Every Flavor Beans did Dumbledore famously taste in the hospital wing, making him swear off them?
What is the magical protection placed on the house where Harry and his parents lived in Godric's Hollow?
The three Unforgivable Curses are Avada Kedavra, Crucio, and what other spell?
What item did Harry's father, James Potter, use to turn into his Animagus form?
options: None, it was an innate ability
quiz.correctAnswer: None, it was an innate ability

quiz.question: In Harry's fifth year, what magical creature does Luna Lovegood mention that Harry and his friends initially doubt the existence of?
What item did Alastor 'Mad-Eye' Moody use to detect magical concealment and Dark Objects on students?
What is the correct incantation for the spell Professor McGonagall uses to animate the statues of Hogwarts in the final battle?
What was the name of the lake where the second task of the Triwizard Tournament took place?
What position did Percy Weasley hold at the Ministry of Magic right after graduating from Hogwarts?
options: Junior Assistant to the Minister for Magic
Head of the Department of Magical Games and Sports
quiz.correctAnswer: Junior Assistant to the Minister for Magic

quiz.question: Which of the founders of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry left the school after a disagreement with the others?
Who was the witch who originally owned the Time-Turner that Hermione used to attend extra classes?
options: None, it was a Ministry object
quiz.correctAnswer: None, it was a Ministry object
